clearedSpotChecks.check: Address-keyed rules that the fresh-address runs could not meet (lead L-810): Arc's check on every call that carries value (F-125), Avalanche's fold of bit 248 of storage indexes onto existing slots (F-040), Tempo's transfer policies, MegaETH's per-account accounting, and any compile or cache decision keyed by address, code hash or use count.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Avalanche part rechecked on chain via https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc at latest. eth_getStorageAt of the real PoolManager 0x06380c0e0912312b5150364b9dc4542ba0dbbc85 at slot 0 and at slot 0x01 followed by 31 zero bytes both return the owner 0x47eb0cf11a1626462da3c830bcde64c3f582b5a6, and extsload(bytes32) (selector 0x1e2eaeaf) of the folded index returns the same word, so the fold is live and reaches the PoolManager. Slot 2 and its folded partner both read 0. The fold does not change any PoolManager result. Its fixed slots 0 to 6 have a zero first byte. Every other slot is a keccak256 output or such an output plus a small struct offset (src/libraries/Pool.sol, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol, src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol), so two used slots meet under the fold only if two hashes agree in 255 bits, which no caller can arrange. extsload only reads (src/Extsload.sol:10-38). The clear rests on this argument more than on the 1,256 scripts, which cannot reach colliding slots in any case. The hook-author hazard stays recorded as F-040 (pool-creator). The Monad compiled path is not reachable through eth_call, as the item says, so that part stays open as F-130 records.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1, set 2 at the real address: Tempo differs on 35 scripts, 29 of them native payouts that fail with WrappedError(recipient, 0, revert data, NativeTransferFailed) because Tempo has no native asset; this is the PoolManager having no native balance, not a change in an amount the code computes.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Rechecked on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz. eth_getBalance returns the same placeholder 0x9612...c9b2 (the 4242...42 constant) for the real PoolManager 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 and for 0x...dEaD. An eth_call with value 1 to an account without code and an eth_call of settle() (0x11da60b4) with value 1 to the real PoolManager are both rejected with 'value transfer not allowed' (code -32003). settle() without value reverts with 0x54e3ca0d (ManagerLocked), so the node runs the PoolManager normally. Code path: sync of address(0) only resets the synced currency and never reads the native balance (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288); native take sends value with call at src/types/Currency.sol:48 and reverts through NativeTransferFailed on failure, which also undoes the debit booked at src/PoolManager.sol:294. A positive native delta can only come from msg.value, which no public transaction can carry, so the placeholder balance cannot be spent. This agrees with the cycle 1 and cycle 3 Tempo clears in state/cleared.json.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3. At the real address of each network, scripts/tslots.py read IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT, NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT, RESERVES_OF_SLOT, CURRENCY_SLOT and driver delta slots by exttload at latest and pending, inside one simulated unlock sequence, and as persistent slots; 21 of 21 pass.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Rechecked independently with exttload(bytes32) (selector 0xf135baaa) at the real PoolManager address on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum One, Polygon, Avalanche and Tempo: IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT 0xc090...ab23 (src/libraries/Lock.sol:8) at latest and NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT 0x7d4b...9a0b (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10) at pending both read 0 on all six. Monad answered HTTP 429 and was not rechecked. The in-call order the item reports matches the source: sync writes CURRENCY_SLOT and RESERVES_OF_SLOT and only settle or a native sync clears them (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-29, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). The limit of the method is that an eth_call starts from a fresh transaction context, so it cannot show transient storage surviving from one mined transaction into the next in the same block. That question is covered by other entries in state/cleared.json (client readings of where transient storage is discarded between transactions), so this item claims no more than its method shows.
